recognize_zh: 周邊血中一顆嗜酸性球，細胞質充滿橘紅色粗顆粒，細胞核兩葉在上方凹陷、下方併攏成心形（heart-shaped nucleus）；這是雙葉核尚未完全分開的正常形態變異，不代表病理意義，背景紅血球中央淡染區偏大。
features: Single eosinophil slightly larger than surrounding red cells
Cytoplasm packed with coarse refractile orange-red granules
Nucleus with two incompletely separated lobes forming a heart shape
Background red cells with prominent central pallor and a few larger polychromatic cells
describe_en: Peripheral blood smear shows an eosinophil with coarse orange-red cytoplasmic granules and a nucleus composed of two incompletely separated lobes that together form a heart shape. The chromatin is moderately condensed without nucleoli, and the granules are evenly distributed. Background red cells show prominent central pallor with a few larger polychromatic forms. Findings represent a heart-shaped eosinophil, a normal morphologic variant of bilobed eosinophil nuclear segmentation without specific clinical significance.

ddx.vs: Pelger-Huet cells show symmetric spectacle-shaped bilobed or round nuclei with very coarse chromatin across all granulocytes, not an isolated heart-shaped eosinophil.
Basophil granules are dark purple-black and obscure the nucleus, unlike the orange-red eosinophilic granules here.
Toxic granules are dark blue-purple and finer, in neutrophils with three to five nuclear lobes.
Dysplastic eosinophils show hypogranularity, vacuolization or basophilic-staining granules, which are absent here.
